strings.name: Bonnie Chan
strings.summary: Bonnie Chan is a Hong Kong financial executive and lawyer who has served as CEO of Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing since March 2024. She previously led IPO vetting and listing operations and served as co-chief operating officer. Earlier, she worked in capital markets at investment banks and an international law firm.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026, with the November 6 results announcement as recent evidence. Conflicting birth-year information remains unresolved. Effective dates, announcements and future renewal terms are distinguished, as are company results and individual contributions.
strings.influence.rationale: Promotes listing regulation and capital-market development at HKEX, contributing to Hong Kong's international financial centre.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: She graduated from the University of Hong Kong's law faculty in 1991 and Harvard Law School in 1993, earning an LLB and an LLM respectively.
strings.facts.f2.label: Professional qualifications
strings.facts.f2.value: She is qualified as a Hong Kong solicitor and a New York State attorney. Her LLM is not a doctorate or an MBA.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Legal and listing experience
strings.highlights.h1.text: Her experience spans private practice, investment-bank legal departments and the exchange, including listing review, rules and operational management.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Multi-asset market development
strings.highlights.h2.text: As CEO, she advances products and market infrastructure. Reforms involve the exchange's teams, regulators and market participants working together.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Comments on quarterly results
strings.timeline.t1.text: The announcement includes her views on market development. Third-quarter profit attributable to shareholders was HK$4.859 billion, down 1% year on year, distinct from nine-month records.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Next term approved
strings.timeline.t2.text: The board and SFC approve a further three-year term from March 1, 2027 to February 28, 2030. It had not started by the review cutoff.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Becomes CEO
strings.timeline.t3.text: She succeeds Nicolas Aguzin and becomes an ex-officio director. An earlier announcement brought forward the handover originally planned for May.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Becomes co-chief operating officer
strings.timeline.t4.text: She shares the role with Wilfred Yiu, while Katherine Ng succeeds her as head of listing. January 16 was the announcement date.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Returns to HKEX as head of listing
strings.timeline.t5.text: She succeeds David Graham. The appointment was announced in October 2019 and became effective the following January.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joins Davis Polk as partner
strings.timeline.t6.text: In her 2021 interview, she recalls joining in December to help build its Hong Kong law practice. She remains until 2019.
strings.timeline.t7.title: First joins HKEX
strings.timeline.t7.text: She becomes head of IPO transactions, leading a team reviewing listing applications and contributing to related policy.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Begins solicitor training
strings.timeline.t8.text: After completing her studies at Harvard Law School, she returns to Hong Kong and trains at Deacons.
